before: Blessed and noble, then, are all the martyrdoms that have taken place according to the will of God. For we must be reverent and assign to God authority over all things.

Who would not marvel at their nobility, their endurance, and their love for the Master? They were torn by scourges until the structure of the flesh could be seen down to the inner veins and arteries, yet they endured so steadfastly that even the bystanders wept and grieved. Some of them reached such heights of courage that not one of them cried out or groaned, showing all of us that in that hour of torture the noble martyrs of Christ were absent from the flesh—or rather, that the Lord stood by them and spoke with them.

Fixing their attention on the grace of Christ, they despised the torments of this world, purchasing eternal life at the cost of a single hour. The fire of their savage torturers felt cold to them, for they kept before their eyes the eternal life that is never quenched, and with the eyes of their hearts they gazed upon the good things reserved for those who endure—things no ear has heard, no eye has seen, and no human heart has conceived. But these were shown to them by the Lord, for they were no longer human beings but already angels.

In the same way, those condemned to the wild beasts endured terrible punishments: they were bound to stakes and tormented with other forms of varied tortures, so that the tyrant might, if possible, turn them to denial through relentless punishment. For the devil schemed many things against them.

before: So they took the boy, and on the Preparation day, around the dinner hour, the pursuers and cavalry went out with their usual weapons, running as if they were chasing a robber. Late in the hour they closed in on him and found him lying down in an upper room. He could have gone from there to another place, but he refused. He said, “The will of God be done.”

When he heard that they had arrived, he came down and talked with them. Those present marveled at his age and his calm steadfastness, and at the fact that there was such eagerness to arrest so old a man. At once he ordered food and drink to be set before them at that hour, as much as they wanted, and he asked them to give him an hour to pray without fear.

They granted it, and he stood and prayed, so full of the grace of God that for two hours he could not be silent. Those who heard him were astonished, and many regretted that they had come against such a godly old man.

before: The proconsul kept pressing him. "Swear by Caesar's fortune," he said.

Polycarp answered, "If you imagine in your vanity that I will swear by Caesar's fortune, as you put it, and if you pretend not to know who I am, then listen plainly: I am a Christian. And if you want to learn the teaching of Christianity, give me a day and listen."

Polycarp replied, "You I would have considered worthy of an answer, for we have been taught to give to rulers and authorities appointed by God the honor that is fitting, as long as it does us no harm. But those people I do not consider worthy of making a defense to them."
